script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 29. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You're never alone.  Right now, trillions of microorganisms live on your skin, in your gut, in your mouth.  You host more bacterial cells than human cells.

Your body hosts about 38 trillion bacteria—slightly outnumbering your 30 trillion human cells. By cell count, you're barely half human. Add viruses and fungi, and you're a walking ecosystem, not just an organism. Gut bacteria break down fiber you can't digest, produce vitamins you need, and train your immune system.  Without them, you'd be malnourished and vulnerable to infection.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Scale changes everything.  Most of life exists at sizes we can't see.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Invisible Appreciation - Honor What You Can't See.

Here's your activity: Your microbiome works constantly—digesting, protecting, producing. What other invisible systems do you depend on daily? Infrastructure, relationships, processes that run unseen? The invisible often matters more than the visible. This helps you appreciate invisible but essential systems.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about tiny life everywhere can be applied to invisible appreciation - honor what you can't see. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
